name: send-chat-message
description:
Send a new chatMessage in the specified chat. This API can't create a new chat; you must use the list chats method to retrieve the ID of an existing chat before you can create a chat message.

💡 TIP: To @mention someone, put <at user-id="<aad-user-id>">Display Name</at> in the html content; the server numbers the tag and builds the mentions array. Each mention id must match its <at id> value; include userIdentityType: 'aadUser' or Graph returns 400 'value without a type name'.

messageHistory.description: List of activity history of a message item, including modification time and actions, such as reactionAdded, reactionRemoved, or reaction changes, on the message.

reactions.description: Reactions for this chat message (for example, Like).

subject.description: The subject of the chat message, in plaintext.

summary.description: Summary text of the chat message that could be used for push notifications and summary views or fall back views. Only applies to channel chat messages, not chat messages in a chat.

hostedContents.description: Content in a message hosted by Microsoft Teams - for example, images or code snippets.

replies.description: Replies for a specified message. Supports $expand for channel messages.

teamId.description: Value for the 'teamId' path segment. Pass it under the name 'teamId', not as 'id'. Use the 'id' field of the team object as returned by Microsoft Graph.

channelId.description: Value for the 'channelId' path segment. Pass it under the name 'channelId', not as 'id'. Use the 'id' field of the channel object as returned by Microsoft Graph.

chatMessageId.description: Value for the 'chatMessageId' path segment. Pass it under the name 'chatMessageId', not as 'id'. Use the 'id' field of the chat message object as returned by Microsoft Graph.

includeHeaders.description: Include response headers (including ETag) in the response metadata

excludeResponse.description: Exclude the full response body and only return success or failure indication

name: list-team-members
description:
Get the conversationMember collection of a team. The membership IDs returned by the server must be treated as opaque strings. The client shouldn't try to parse or make assumptions about these resource IDs. In the future, membership results can include users from various tenants, as indicated in the response. Clients should avoid assuming that all members exclusively belong to the current tenant.

💡 TIP: Lists members of a team. Each member has displayName, email, roles and userId. Pass name to keep only members whose displayName or email contains that text (case-insensitive); use the returned userId in an @mention.

top.description: Page size (Graph $top). Start small (e.g. 5–15) so responses fit the model context; raise only if needed. Use $select to return fewer fields per item. For more rows, use @odata.nextLink from the response instead of a very large $top.

skip.description: Items to skip for pagination. Not supported with $search.

search.description: KQL search query in one pair of double quotes; directory (users/groups) instead quotes each clause with no outer pair. Cannot combine with $filter.

filter.description: OData filter expression. Add $count=true for advanced filters (flag/flagStatus, contains()). Cannot combine with $search.

count.description: Set true to enable advanced query mode (ConsistencyLevel: eventual). Required for complex $filter on flag/flagStatus or contains(). The response then includes @odata.count, the total for the filtered collection, which can exceed the items returned when fetchAllPages hits its page/item cap.

select.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. id,subject,from,receivedDateTime

expand.description: Navigation properties to inline, e.g. attachments on a message or event. Only navigation properties can be expanded: expanding a non-navigation property such as a message body fails with "Parsing OData Select and Expand failed". Request ordinary fields with $select instead. Some APIs accept only one relationship per request, so prefer a single value. Some relationships support nested selection, e.g. children($select=id,name).

teamId.description: Value for the 'teamId' path segment. Pass it under the name 'teamId', not as 'id'. Use the 'id' field of the team object as returned by Microsoft Graph.

fetchAllPages.description: Follow @odata.nextLink and merge up to 100 pages into one response. Can return enormous payloads—only when the user explicitly needs a full export. Prefer a small $top first, then paginate or narrow with $filter/$search.

name.description: Case-insensitive text to match against each member's displayName and email. Applied after $select projection, so only fields you can see are matched. Without fetchAllPages only the fetched page is filtered, and @odata.count still reports the unfiltered total.

skiptoken.description: Next page: the @odata.nextLink from the previous response. Keep the other arguments the same.

includeHeaders.description: Include response headers (including ETag) in the response metadata

excludeResponse.description: Exclude the full response body and only return success or failure indication

name: parse-teams-url
description: Converts any Teams meeting URL format (short /meet/, full /meetup-join/, or recap ?threadId=) into a standard joinWebUrl. Use this before list-online-meetings when the user provides a recap or short URL.

url.description: Teams meeting URL in any format

name: read-mail-text
description: Triage view of up to 20 mail messages at once, as text with the bulk junk removed: invisible padding, image placeholders and quoted reply history (forwards keep theirs). Links are kept: Safe Links, Proofpoint and Google redirects are unwrapped to the real address and tracking parameters (utm_* and similar) dropped; only an address still over 300 characters (a tracking redirect) is shortened to ⟦link: domain⟧. Everything else (signatures, footers, whitespace) is left as the message has it; line endings become \n and ⟦ ⟧ in the body itself appear as [ ]. Use get-mail-message for the raw body or the quoted thread. Give messageIds (up to 20), or folderId with optional top and filter or search for the newest messages in a folder. Each message is cut to maxChars characters (default 3,000; marked truncated: true): pass a larger maxChars, up to 300,000, for the whole of a long message; a body over 300,000 characters is cleaned only that far. If the whole result would exceed the server limit (MS365_MCP_READ_MAIL_TEXT_MAX_CHARS, default 80000) the call fails, listing the largest messages, instead of returning part of it. Returns [{ id, from, to, cc, subject, received, hasAttachments, text, chars, truncated }].

messageIds.description: Ids of the messages to read (max 20). Give messageIds or folderId, not both.

folderId.description: Folder to read from: a well-known name (inbox, sentitems, drafts, archive, deleteditems, junkemail) or a folder id.

top.description: With folderId: how many messages, newest first (default and max 20).

filter.description: With folderId: OData $filter, e.g. receivedDateTime ge 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z or from/emailAddress/address eq 'a@example.com'.

search.description: With folderId: KQL search, e.g. from:paul subject:"quarterly report" (quoting is normalised as for list-mail-messages). Graph cannot combine it with filter.

maxChars.description: Cut each message text to this many characters (marked truncated). Default 3,000; pass up to 300,000 for the whole of a long message (a body over 300,000 characters is cleaned only that far, also marked truncated).

name: get-download-url
description: Resolve a short-lived, pre-authenticated download URL for Microsoft Graph binary content that exposes one (drive/SharePoint file content). The returned URL streams the bytes with NO Authorization header, so the client can fetch it straight to disk (e.g. curl) without round-tripping base64 through the agent context. Prefer this over download-bytes for any file above a few KB or any bulk download. Returns { downloadUrl, name?, size?, contentType? }. Mail file attachments (/messages/{id}/attachments/{id}/$value), meeting recordings and other $value byte endpoints have no pre-authenticated URL from Graph itself, but call this tool for them anyway: a server running with --enable-attachment-urls mints its own single-use URL for them, and one without it answers with the reason and points at download-bytes.

target.description: Relative Microsoft Graph path starting with "/". Either a driveItem content path or the item path itself, e.g. /drives/{drive-id}/items/{driveItem-id}/content, /me/drive/items/{driveItem-id}/content, or /sites/{site-id}/drive/items/{driveItem-id}. A trailing /content is optional and is stripped automatically for drive items. Mail attachment $value paths and meeting recordings are accepted on a server running with --enable-attachment-urls.
